terms.gloss: What do you advise? What do you recommend?
terms.comment: Suādeō takes the thing advised in the accusative, “to advise, recommend” (Lewis & Short). Add mihi or nōbīs, and name the choices if there are any.

terms.gloss: What do you advise me to do?
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.40.2: etsī quid mī auctor es? advolōne an maneō?
terms.comment: Cicero’s question to Atticus about a course of action, “what do you advise?”; see “advice” for tē auctōre.

phrases.latin: Quid nōbīs suādēs, piscemne an agnīnam?
phrases.english: What do you recommend, the fish or the lamb?

phrases.latin: nunc mihi quid suādēs post damnum temporis et spēs dēceptās?
phrases.english: now what do you advise me, after the time I have lost and the hopes that have failed me?

phrases.latin: etsī quid mī auctor es? advolōne an maneō?
phrases.english: but what do you advise? Shall I hurry to you, or stay?

sources: Lewis & Short: suadeo · Lewis & Short: auctor
